question.knowledge_point: Calculating an Element of the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
question.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $39.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-1-0) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23}=\frac{1}{39}\cdot 1=\frac{1}{39}.\end{aligned}
$$
